site.name: orbitride
site.summary: orbitride-clone Fictional intercity rideshare / bus booking flow "OrbitRide". Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing: search box (From / To city autocomplete datalist, date, passengers) + 3 value props + 6 popular-route cards | | `routes.html` | Trip results list: left filters (time-of-day, price slider, 4 amenities multi-select); top 7-day date carousel; 8 trip rows (carrier, departure–arrival, duration, stops, amenities, seats left, price, Select button) | | `seats.html` | SVG bus seat map: front 2 priority rows, middle 11 standard 2+2 rows, rear 5-seat row; selectable count = passengers; occupied / selected / standard / priority states; right side legend + selected list + price box + Continue |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full orbitride system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The OrbitRide booking flow suffers from critical mobile usability issues, primarily horizontal overflow on the routes page that forces users to scroll sideways to access 'Select' buttons. Additionally, the seat selection interface lacks clear affordances for touch interaction, and the system relies on passive disabled states rather than active feedback when users attempt to proceed with incomplete selections. Several utility features, such as copying passenger details, appear non-functional, adding friction to multi-passenger bookings.

exploration_plan.goal: Execute a comprehensive UX audit of the OrbitRide booking flow, validating the end-to-end journey from search to confirmation while identifying usability friction points and mobile responsiveness issues.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will simulate a user booking a multi-passenger trip, starting with the landing page search, moving through route filtering, interactive seat selection, passenger details, and payment. It will specifically target high-risk interactions like the SVG seat map and date carousel, ensuring state persistence across steps. Finally, it will repeat critical path checks on a mobile viewport to address known tap-target warnings.
assumptions: The 'FROM' and 'TO' inputs rely on HTML datalists for autocomplete as indicated by the prescan.
The seat map on seats.html is an interactive SVG where clicking toggles selection state.
Navigation between pages relies on standard form submissions or JS-driven href changes without complex SPA routing.
The 'Popular routes' cards on index.html are clickable shortcuts that pre-fill the search form.
risk_hotspots: seats.html: SVG seat map interaction (selection logic, occupied vs available states)
routes.html: Filter sidebar behavior (price slider, amenity checkboxes) and date carousel navigation
index.html: Mobile tap targets for header links (known small dimensions in prescan)
passengers.html: Form validation for required fields and error state visibility

phases.title: Search & Discovery
phases.objective: Validate entry points, search form functionality, and result listing filters.
key_checks: Test autocomplete/datalist behavior on FROM/TO inputs.
Click a 'Popular route' card to verify pre-filled search state.
On routes.html, toggle at least two filters (e.g., 'Wi-Fi', 'Morning') and observe list updates.
Navigate the 7-day date carousel to ensure price/route updates.
exit_criteria: Successfully filtered results and selected a specific trip via the 'Select' button.

phases.title: Seat Selection Logic
phases.objective: Verify the core differentiator: the interactive seat map and selection constraints.
key_checks: Identify and select seats matching the passenger count from Phase 1.
Attempt to select an 'occupied' seat to verify it is disabled.
Toggle selection on/off to verify price box updates dynamically.
Verify the 'Continue' button is disabled until the correct number of seats are chosen.
exit_criteria: Correct number of seats selected and transitioned to passenger details page.

phases.title: Checkout Flow & Validation
phases.objective: Test data entry forms, upsell opportunities, and payment processing UI.
key_checks: Submit passenger form with empty required fields to trigger validation errors.
Review 'Extras' page (if present) and toggle an add-on service.
Enter mock payment details and verify input masking/formatting.
Check for clear summary of total cost before final submission.
exit_criteria: Reached confirmation page with a valid booking reference.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Recovery
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical flows on mobile viewport and test navigation recovery.
key_checks: Verify header navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or remains accessible.
Re-test the 'Find rides' button and filter toggles for touch accessibility.
Check if the SVG seat map scales correctly or becomes unusable on small screens.
Use browser back-button from payment page to ensure cart/state isn't lost unexpectedly.
exit_criteria: Critical paths verified on mobile; layout breaks or unclickable elements documented.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 7 HTML files in the site directory.
coverage_targets.features: Interact with search autocomplete, route filters, seat map SVG, and payment form inputs.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 2 interactions on mobile viewport to check for layout shifts and touch target issues.

notes: Prescan noted network errors for Google Fonts; ignore these unless they cause layout shifts (CLS).
Pay close attention to the 'small_tap_target' warnings on index.html during the mobile phase.
If the 'Extras' page is skipped in the default flow, attempt to find a link or query param that forces it.

findings.user_goal: Select a trip from the results list on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Horizontal overflow hides primary action buttons, forcing unnecessary scrolling.
findings.evidence: On mobile viewport (390px), the routes page content width is 760px. The 'Select' buttons are positioned at the far right edge of the trip cards, requiring the user to horizontally scroll to see and tap them. Layout warnings confirm this overflow.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on a vertical list is a significant anti-pattern in mobile UX. It increases cognitive load, makes comparison difficult, and often leads to missed actions or frustration as users struggle to locate interactive elements.
findings.suggestion: Refactor the trip card layout for mobile to stack information vertically or ensure the 'Select' button is always visible within the initial viewport width without horizontal scrolling. Consider a sticky 'Book' button or a full-width card design.

findings.user_goal: Select a specific seat on the bus map.
findings.problem: SVG seat map elements lack clear touch targets and visual feedback on mobile.
findings.evidence: Automated clicks on seats (e.g., seat-1a, ux-seat-4a) frequently timed out or failed, suggesting small hit areas or DOM mapping issues. Visually, the seats are small distinct shapes without generous padding, making them difficult to tap accurately on touch screens.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot reliably select a seat due to small hit targets, they will experience high error rates and frustration. This is a critical blocker in the checkout flow.
findings.suggestion: Increase the clickable area of each seat by adding transparent padding around the SVG shapes or using larger graphical representations. Ensure immediate visual feedback (color change) upon successful tap to confirm selection.

findings.user_goal: Proceed to the next step after selecting seats.
findings.problem: Passive error prevention via disabled buttons provides no active guidance.
findings.evidence: When attempting to click 'Continue' without selecting seats, the button is simply disabled (grayed out). No toast message, shake animation, or tooltip appears to explain why the action failed or what is missing.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may not understand why the button is unclickable, especially if they believe they have completed the task. Active feedback reduces confusion and guides the user toward the correct action.
findings.suggestion: If the user taps the disabled 'Continue' button, trigger a brief haptic feedback or display a tooltip/toast saying 'Please select 2 seats to continue.'

findings.user_goal: Quickly fill out details for multiple passengers.
findings.problem: The 'Copy contact from passenger 1' feature appears non-functional.
findings.evidence: Session logs indicate that clicking 'Copy contact from passenger 1' did not populate Passenger 2's fields, forcing manual re-entry of identical data.
findings.why_it_matters: This feature is a key efficiency tool for group bookings. When it fails, it adds unnecessary friction and time to the checkout process, increasing the likelihood of abandonment.
findings.suggestion: Debug the JavaScript logic behind the copy function to ensure it correctly maps and populates the target fields. Add a visual confirmation (e.g., a checkmark or 'Copied!' text) when the action succeeds.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site using touch controls.
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements have tap targets below the recommended 44px minimum.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag elements like amenity checkboxes (13x13px), header links (21-28px height), and the 'OrbitRide' logo (27px height) as being too small for reliable touch interaction.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets lead to accidental clicks and difficulty for users with motor impairments or those using larger fingers. This violates basic mobile accessibility guidelines.
findings.suggestion: Increase the CSS padding or size of these interactive elements to meet the 44x44px minimum touch target guideline. Use pseudo-elements if necessary to expand the clickable area without changing the visual design.

gaps: Only directly exercised 53% of visible interactive feature signatures.
